claims.text: HEA intermediate layers currently have limited heat-transfer capability while providing moderate structural integrity.
Plasma-facing reactor components experience high temperatures and high heat fluxes.
The proposed benefit should hold from 600°C to 1000°C under thermal cycling and mechanical loading typical of plasma-facing components.
HEAs and related complex concentrated alloys can be subjected to annealing or post-deformation heat treatment.
Tailored cooling and annealing will induce coherent nanoprecipitates of a high-thermal-conductivity intermetallic phase in the HEA matrix.
The induced nanoprecipitates will form an interconnected, percolative lamellar network.
The precipitate network will provide enhanced pathways for phonon transport.
The precipitate network will provide enhanced pathways for electron transport.
Coherent precipitate–matrix interfaces will preserve the inherent strength of the HEA matrix.
Non-coherent or excessive phase separation produces thermal or mechanical trade-offs that coherent nanoprecipitation can avoid.
Tailored thermal processing will significantly increase thermal conductivity relative to conventionally treated HEA intermediate layers.
The thermal-conductivity improvement will occur without degrading mechanical strength or structural integrity under high-temperature, high-load conditions.
The improvement depends on obtaining an optimal nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and coherence.
Excessive or incoherent precipitate formation may eliminate the heat-transfer benefit or degrade mechanical performance.
